goal_text: (Reused from research_synth_007) Compare aerobic and anaerobic respiration on three dimensions: ATP yield, cellular location, and byproducts.
ground_truth: Aerobic respiration occurs in the mitochondria, yields 36-38 ATP per glucose molecule, and produces carbon dioxide and water as byproducts. Anaerobic respiration (glycolysis) occurs in the cytoplasm, yields only 2 ATP per glucose, and produces lactic acid (in animals and bacteria) or ethanol and CO2 (in yeast). Aerobic respiration is approximately 18 times more energy-efficient.
